_comment: Machine-readable source of truth for every retention period J'Toye publishes (LGL-01 / D-07). Each row was read out of its enforcement site on the date below, not carried forward from a prior document. Two gates close the loop: scripts/check-retention-enforcement.sh asserts tree -> manifest (every Automated row names a site that exists, holds the declared value converted to the published unit, and has a consumer that actually reads it), and scripts/gates/claims.manifest asserts manifest -> published prose. The flat integer keys below exist so the claim-gate engine can read them: its json source does a top-level has($k) lookup, which errors on a bare array. The full rows live under .rows.
_legal_status: Every lawful-basis statement here is a legal position and needs adviser confirmation before it is relied upon. The periods themselves are measurements and are gated. No statutory retention figure is published as a number anywhere in this file - see R-9.

rows.detail: An order you started but never paid for, including the name, email and phone number typed into the checkout form.
rows.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) - holding an in-progress basket long enough for you to come back and finish it, then deleting it.
rows.note: Deleted, not anonymised. A daily 03:00 UTC job removes every DRAFT order past the cutoff, one transaction per tenant.

rows.detail: The log of each outbound webhook a vendor's integration was sent, including the delivery attempt history.
rows.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) - letting a vendor debug a failed integration delivery, bounded so the log does not become an open-ended store.
rows.note: Scoped to webhook_delivery ONLY. The same job deliberately never touches suppression or opt-in rows - see R-6.

rows.detail: The raw bytes of an image a vendor uploaded, held in quarantine while the pipeline validates and re-encodes it. Only the validated derivative is kept afterwards; the raw upload is reclaimed.
rows.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) - a declared horizon that lets a vendor's upload survive a broker outage instead of being destroyed as a 15-minute accident, while still bounding how long unvalidated bytes sit on the origin.
rows.note: The site stores 259200000 milliseconds; the published period is 72 hours. The unit conversion is owned by scripts/check-retention-enforcement.sh because the claim-gate engine has no unit transform, so an un-converted comparison would silently never match.

rows.detail: The jtoye-customer-refresh and jtoye-customer-id cookies that keep you signed in to a shop between visits.
rows.lawful_basis: Strictly necessary (PECR reg. 6(4)) - these cookies exist only to deliver the sign-in you asked for; no consent is required and none is sought.
rows.note: Browser-enforced by Max-Age. This is a cap: the effective limit can be shorter, because the identity provider's own session idle and maximum lifespans also apply.

rows.detail: The short-lived jtoye-customer-access cookie carrying the access token for the current request.
rows.period_display: The short sign-in session length set by our identity provider, renewed automatically while you stay signed in
rows.lawful_basis: Strictly necessary (PECR reg. 6(4)) - required to deliver the signed-in session you asked for.
rows.note: Enforced, but the number is not ours. The cookie's Max-Age is derived from the identity provider realm's access-token lifespan, which lives in the IdP and not in this repository. Publishing it as a hard number, or gating it against a value this repo does not own, would become a false statement the first time the realm changes - so it is described and deliberately NOT gated.

rows.detail: The record that you unsubscribed from a category, or that you opted in to marketing.
rows.lawful_basis: Legal obligation and legitimate interests (UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(c) and 6(1)(f)) - an opt-out that expired would resurrect a suppressed recipient, so honouring it permanently is the obligation, not an option.
rows.note: Published as an Automated NEGATIVE: the gate asserts that no prune, purge or delete path exists against notification_suppression or marketing_opt_in, and carries a positive control proving the same scan shape does find the prune path that exists for webhook_delivery. V54's header states it directly: 'A GDPR/PECR opt-out must NOT expire, so - unlike webhook_delivery - there is deliberately no retention window / prune job on suppression (threat T-22-02-04).' Both tables are bounded by their UNIQUE key instead of by time.

rows.category: Your personal details on completed orders
rows.detail: Your name, email, phone and delivery address as they appear on orders, customer records and reviews.
rows.period_display: Removed on request - there is no automatic timer
rows.lawful_basis: Right to erasure (UK GDPR Art. 17), applied by anonymising rather than deleting so the vendor's financial record stays intact.
rows.note: Executed by the shipped erasure path in uk.jtoye.core.gdpr, which anonymises rather than deletes and writes a PII-free proof row. Marked Operational because it runs when a request is made, not on a schedule a gate could read a period out of.

rows.detail: The append-only history of changes to records, used to answer who changed what and when.
rows.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) - integrity, dispute resolution and security investigation. Personal data inside this history is scrubbed when an erasure request is honoured (R-7).
rows.note: No deletion path exists anywhere for audit history. The Article-17 scrub edits it in place rather than removing rows.

rows.detail: Completed orders and the financial transactions recorded against them.
rows.period_display: For as long as the law requires
rows.lawful_basis: Legal obligation (UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(c)) - tax and accounting record-keeping.
rows.note: NO NUMBER IS PUBLISHED HERE ON PURPOSE. A statutory figure would be a legal position, not a measurement, and this repository enforces no deletion path for these records at all. Publishing a specific number of years without adviser confirmation would put an unverified claim in a legally operative document.

rows.detail: The email address you type to look up an order, kept in your browser's session storage so the page does not ask again while you are on it.
rows.period_display: Cleared when you close the tab
rows.lawful_basis: Strictly necessary (PECR reg. 6(4)) - it exists only to deliver the order lookup you asked for, and never reaches our servers as a stored record.
rows.note: Browser-enforced by sessionStorage semantics, which is exactly why it is gateable: if this were ever changed to localStorage the published claim would become false, and the anchored literal assertion fires.

rows.category: Saved checkout email in your browser
rows.detail: The email address you last used at a shop's checkout, kept in your browser's local storage so it can be filled in for you next time.
rows.period_display: Until you clear your browser's site data
rows.lawful_basis: Strictly necessary (PECR reg. 6(4)) - it is a convenience within the checkout you asked for, stays on your device, and is never read by us as a stored record.
rows.note: Local storage has no expiry, so there is nothing on our side that deletes it: you control it. Marked Operational rather than Automated for exactly that reason - claiming an automated period here would be false.

rows.category: Guest order history in your browser
rows.detail: The list of orders you placed as a guest, kept in your browser's local storage so you can find them again without an account.
rows.period_display: Until you clear your browser's site data
rows.lawful_basis: Strictly necessary (PECR reg. 6(4)) - it is what lets a guest find the order they just placed, and it stays on your device.
rows.note: Same shape as R-12: no expiry exists on our side, so no automated period may be claimed.

deliberately_unpublished.reason: The configuration key cleanup.orphaned-image-days declared a 7-day deletion that NOTHING performed. Verified two-arm on 2026-08-16 with an identically shaped live control: the key had zero Java consumers (rc=1, empty) while the control key cleanup.stale-draft-hours returned a hit under identical flags, globs and directory (rc=0). Publishing it would have put a false statement in a legally operative document, and leaving it in configuration invited someone to publish it later - so the key was deleted from application.yml and from .planning/codebase/INTEGRATIONS.md rather than published.
